column2: Competition Commission of India v. State of Mizoram & Ors.
column3: Civil Appeal Nos. 10820-10822 of 2014 (with C.A. No. 1797 of 2015)
column11: s 3(1) r/w s 3(3)(d) Competition Act (bid rigging); s 2(u) (service)
column12: Whether the CCI can inquire into bid rigging in tenders for lottery distributors when lotteries are res extra commercium.
column13: Yes. The regulated status of lotteries does not take collusive tendering out of the Act; the Gauhati HC judgment was set aside and the CCI inquiry against the bidders continues (paras 43-44).
column14: CCI v. Bharti Airtel Ltd. (2019) 2 SCC 521

column2: Coal India Ltd. & Anr. v. Competition Commission of India & Anr.
column11: s 2(h) and s 4 r/w s 19(4)(g) Competition Act
column12: Whether the Competition Act applies to Coal India despite the Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1973 and Art 39(b).
column13: It does. A government company holding a statutory monopoly is an enterprise and is not exempt; the appeal was directed to be heard on its own merits (paras 125-126).
column14: Ashoka Smokeless Coal India (P) Ltd. v. Union of India (2007) 2 SCC 640

column2: Independent Sugar Corporation Ltd. v. Girish Sriram Juneja & Ors.
column3: 2025 INSC 124 (Civil Appeal No. 6071 of 2023 and connected appeals)
column11: proviso to s 31(4) IBC r/w ss 6 and 29 Competition Act
column12: Whether CCI approval of a combination must be obtained before the CoC approves an insolvency resolution plan.
column13: Prior CCI approval is mandatory, not directory. The AGI Greenpac plan was quashed and the CoC directed to reconsider plans that had CCI approval (paras 155-158; S.V.N. Bhatti J. wrote separately).
column14: Committee of Creditors of Essar Steel India Ltd. v. Satish Kumar Gupta (2020) 8 SCC 531

column2: Competition Commission of India v. Schott Glass India Pvt. Ltd. & Anr.
column3: 2025 INSC 668 (Civil Appeal No. 5843 of 2014 with C.A. No. 9998 of 2014)
column12: Whether Schott's volume rebates, long-term supply agreement and alleged tying were an abuse of dominant position.
column13: No abuse established. An effects-based analysis is obligatory in every s 4 inquiry (para 66(i)), and refusing cross-examination vitiated the DG's findings (paras 75, 77); appeals dismissed (para 79).
column14: Excel Crop Care Ltd. v. CCI (2017) 8 SCC 47

column2: Competition Commission of India v. Independent Sugar Corporation Ltd. & Anr.
column3: R.P.(C) No. 482 of 2025 in Civil Appeal No. 4924 of 2023
column11: s 29(1) and s 29(1A) Competition Act; Reg 25(1A) Combination Regulations
column12: Whether s 29 requires the CCI to send every combination to the DG after issuing a show cause notice.
column13: No. A show cause notice under s 29(1) is mandatory, but a DG reference under s 29(1A) is discretionary; paras 128-131 of the 29-01-2025 judgment were replaced by paras 10-11 of the review order.
column14: P.T. Rajan v. T.P.M. Sahir (2003) 8 SCC 498

column2: Competition Commission of India v. Monsanto Holdings Pvt. Ltd. & Ors.
column12: Whether the CCI probe into patent licensing terms could continue after the informants settled with the patentees.
column13: The Court declined to interfere with the Delhi HC judgment of 13-07-2023, accepting that the settlement removed the substratum of the probe, and kept the Patents Act versus Competition Act question open.
column14: Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson v. CCI (Delhi HC, LPA 247 of 2016, 13-07-2023), para 58

column2: Competition Commission of India v. Kerala Film Exhibitors Federation & Ors.
column11: s 3(1) r/w s 3(3)(b), s 27 and s 48 Competition Act (pre-2023 text)
column12: Whether office-bearers of a trade association were entitled to a second show cause notice on penalty, and whether the penalty was disproportionate.
column13: One notice was enough and the penalty was proportionate (paras 52, 64). The COMPAT order was set aside and the CCI order of 08-09-2015, including the two-year bar on the office-bearers, was restored (para 68).
column14: Excel Crop Care Ltd. v. CCI (2017) 8 SCC 47

column2: Flipkart India Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. v. Competition Commission of India & Anr.
column11: s 4 r/w s 26(1) and s 53B Competition Act
column12: Whether the NCLAT's direction for a DG investigation into Flipkart could stand when it rested on an income tax assessment order no longer in existence.
column13: Appeal allowed in part. The NCLAT order of 04-03-2020 was set aside and the appeal remanded for fresh decision on whether a prima facie case exists, applying Coal India; no view on merits.
column14: Coal India Ltd. v. CCI (2023) 10 SCC 345

column2: Amazon.com NV Investment Holdings LLC v. Competition Commission of India & Ors.
column11: s 45(2) r/w proviso to s 20(1), s 31(1), ss 43A and 44 Competition Act; Reg 5(5) Combination Regulations
column12: Whether the CCI could hold its 2019 approval of the Amazon-Future Coupons combination in abeyance and impose penalties for incomplete disclosure.
column13: No. s 45(2) is a penal provision and gives no power to suspend or reopen an approval, and the action was outside the one-year limit in s 20(1). The NCLAT and CCI orders were set aside and deposits ordered refunded with 6% interest (paras 303-305).
column14: Gorkha Security Services v. Govt. (NCT of Delhi) (2014) 9 SCC 105
